newsitem.title: USA: Michigan cites Home Depot in pricing actions.
newsitem.headline: Michigan cites Home Depot in pricing actions.

text.p: Michigan Attorney General Frank Kelley said on Monday his office filed a Notice of Intended Action charging Home Depot Inc with violating the state's Consumer Protection and Item Pricing and Deceptive Advertising Acts.
The retailer has 10 days to respond to the notice. Otherwise, a lawsuit may be filed to stop the illegal activity. The maximum penalty for knowing and persistent violations of the act is $25,000.

The Notice of Intended Action states that investigators from Kelley's Consumer Protection Division in 1995 found that Home Depot stores in Canton Township, Northville, Pontiac and Utica, Mich. were failing to item price almost all consumer goods as required by law.
When Home Depot was informed of the failures to comply with the law, they gave verbal assurances the stores would be brought into compliance, Kelley said.

In October and November, 1996, investigators found that the stores had failed to comply with the item pricing law. In addition, it found that those items that were priced properly did not reflect the correct price when scanned at the cash register.
Home Depot had no immediate comment but said it would issue a statement later.
